FOOD THAT NOURISHES THE WHOLE HUMAN BEING
CERTIFIED REAL ORGANIC PRODUCE & ANIMAL WELFARE APPROVED, GMO-FREE MEATS
Against the Grain provides Organic produce and Animal Welfare Approved Livestock. 

Against the Grain is a 35 acre diversified farm farm located 15 minutes from downtown Boone, NC in the community of Zionville.  The farm raises a broad spectrum of certified REAL Organic vegetables on about 2 acres of crop land and pasture-raised, GMO-free, Animal Welfare Approved meats on the remaining pastures, woodlots and hay fields.

LEARN MORE
WHAT WE GROW

In 2013, we were introduced to Biodynamic farming practices, which immediately resonated with us as a holistic approach to farming. A Biodynamic farming practice involves creating a diverse and balanced farm ecosystem through on-farm fertility cycling, working with natural and cosmic rhythms, and utilizing preparations consisting of fermented manure, herbs and minerals. 

LIVESTOCK

All of our livestock is pasture-raised, GMO-free, and Animal Welfare Approved and is fed GMO-free feed and has access to unlimited fresh water. 

LEARN MORE
PRODUCE

We raise a broad spectrum of vegetables with only the use of organically certified, OMRI listed inputs.

LEARN MORE
SORGHUM

A traditional Appalachian crop that has been grown for generations. We press the juice from the cane and boil it over a wood fire until the molasses forms.

HOW WE GROW IT

At Against the Grain, we hold the following certifications as a way to verify the integrity of our growing practices: Certified REAL Organic (through the REAL Organic Project), Certified Organic (through One Cert, Inc.), Appalachian Grown and Animal Welfare Approved.  These certifications provide our customers and CSA members with the confidence that the food received from the farm is of the highest nutritional quality and safety, while also being good for the planet.

CATTLE

Against the Grain added cattle to the farm in 2015. We source our weaned steers and heifers from Holly’s Dad, George, who farms in Ashe County. George raises Herefords, the same breed of cattle Holly’s Great-Grandfather raised, on some of the same land that the family has farmed for 200 years. The cattle are raised exclusively on grass and hay and are only fed GMO-free grain as treats.  During the growing season, they are rotated intensively on pastures and hay fields and during the winter they live in a protected paddock with constant fresh water and hay. 

In 2021, by way of a gift from a longtime CSA member and farm supporter, the farm welcomed a small herd of highland cattle to the farm.  The highlands graze a steep hillside and offer their manure for our compost piles, which in turn feed the vegetable crops.

You can find ATG beef at the weekly farmer’s market or by joining our CSA.

What is a CSA and why is it important?

Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) is a way for members to connect directly to their local food system by engaging directly with a local farmer in their area.  In the winter and spring, CSA Members invest in the farm in the form of an advanced payment for vegetables and other farm goods that they will receive during the growing season. This investment helps to ensure the continued presence of farms like ATG in the High Country Community and more deeply connects members to their food and the people who grow it.

At ATG, we are committed to producing high quality, healthy food and fostering food access in the High Country community, regardless of means. We believe that healthy food is a basic human right. Through our CSA Cost Share program neighbors can help neighbors, for none are fed unless all are fed. These relationships nurture not only healthy bodies but also healthy hearts and minds.  In 2025, our goal is to raise enough funds to offer 10 CSA shares at no cost to members of our community! We very much welcome your contribution.

How does CSAWare work?

CSA Ware is a software platform that helps CSA farmers offer their members customizable CSA shares.  When you sign up for an Against the Grain CSA share, you’ll do so under on ATG’s personal sign up page on the CSA Ware website.

Once you sign up, you’ll get to set preferences on all the products we offer. Each week's share will be based on a combination of your preferences and what ATG has available that week. 

Each week during the CSA season, you’ll receive an email with news from the farm as well as a list of the contents of your customized share.  You’ll have 48 hours to further customize your share by removing items and/or adding extras!

What makes CSAWare so great?

CSA members can customize their weekly shares!!

CSA Ware makes it easier for farms like ATG to offer payment plans to our CSA members.  Read more about the payment plans that ATG offers HERE. 

CSA Ware also offers the ability for members to reschedule their share for another week or change pick up locations to accommodate your schedule.

Included in the CSA Ware platform are recipe suggestions, cooking tips, storage, and food prep resources to help reduce food waste and encourage your creativity in the kitchen.

MEET THE FARMERS

Holly Whitesides and Andy Bryant have been farming organically together since 2010.  In the spring of 2012, they bought the land that would become Against the Grain, and in the 2013 growing season, they were introduced to Biodynamic farming practices.  Growing food that nurtures a whole human being, body, soul and spirit, has always been a shared passion for Holly and Andy.  

The Biodynamic approach provides a framework of principles that guide the farm's growth and development in a holistic way.  Holly has been farming full time since 2012, and in October of 2014, the farm welcomed Beatrice Lytton Bryant to the family.  In the spring of 2015, Andy transitioned to farming full time, which has allowed the farm to grow by leaps and bounds.  The farm welcomed two more family members, Corva Lucilla Bryant in April of 2018 and Linnea Marin in January 2021.  We hope that our love of the farm and our passion for growing nutritious food comes through in the products that we offer our community.

Farm Family: Holly, Andy, and Bea
